brief.analysis: The strongest case against fading defense is that the mean has moved: measured against its own rising trend the ratio is barely stretched at all (0.65) even though it looks stretched against a flat five-year average (1.7) — the two readings disagree, direct evidence the normal level is drifting up. That drift is backed by a genuine spending regime change: defense names are up ~55% versus ~17% for the S&P over the past year, prime-contractor backlogs jumped ~24% to $1.36 trillion, and the sector has moved into a structurally higher gear. The old five-year average is an invalid target; this is a trap, not a rubber band.
brief.report_line: Avoid shorting aerospace-and-defense versus the S&P — the ratio looks stretched only against a stale flat average, while rising budgets and record backlogs have permanently lifted the fair level.

brief.analysis: There is almost no edge left to fade here — miners have already reverted to both their one-year and trend-adjusted levels, so the statistical stretch is essentially gone. What remains is a structural metals story working against a short: record central-bank gold buying, physically tight copper, and resource nationalization and supply disruptions have re-rated the group. With the reversion spent and the drivers structural, the old five-year average is not a target worth shorting toward.
brief.report_line: Avoid shorting metals-and-mining versus the S&P — the reversion is already complete and structural forces in gold and copper have reset the group's fair level higher.

brief.analysis: The bet that silver falls back toward gold has already largely played out — silver has come most of the way back and hit its one-year average, leaving little room to the flat five-year mean. The competing force is structural: record central-bank gold buying in 2025 set a floor under gold, so pushing all the way to the old mean assumes a gold pullback that the buyers may not allow. The near-term reversion is real but mostly spent; treat the last leg to the five-year average as optional, not the base case.
brief.report_line: Short silver versus gold is a nearly-complete reversion — most of the move is behind us, and record central-bank gold demand argues against chasing the final leg to the old average.

brief.analysis: The bet is that chipmakers give back their lead over the broad Nasdaq, but the AI build-out is still accelerating — data-center spending by the big cloud firms is set to jump roughly 78% into 2026 — so the gap could stay wide longer than history suggests. Against that, the ratio's own trend line hasn't drifted (the plain and trend-adjusted readings agree) and 6 of 8 past stretches this extreme snapped back within a year, so the five-year average remains a plausible target — just not one to press. Trade it small: the confirmation signals are weak and the short-term uptrend is still working against you.
brief.report_line: Short semiconductors versus the Nasdaq as a half-size fade — history favors reversion, but a still-accelerating AI spending cycle is the reason to keep it small rather than full.
